title: Hypostyle hall + courtyard
region: Early mosque tradition across multiple regions
period: From the seventh century; repeatedly adapted
summary: A column-supported prayer hall beside an open courtyard. Treat it as a spatial lineage with many regional expressions, not a single decorative style.
spatialPrinciples: Repeated structural bays
Broad qibla-side prayer hall
Courtyard as arrival, overflow and environmental buffer
climateAndMaterial: Bay depth, courtyard proportion and openings must respond to the actual climate
Column grid must coordinate prayer rows, sightlines and accessibility
Material is locally specific; the lineage does not prescribe a finish
designMoves: Test the structural grid against saff spacing
Keep an accessible route legible through repeated bays
Model shade, glare, rain and acoustic behavior around the courtyard
avoid: Do not copy columns or capitals without a specific documented reference
Do not assume an open courtyard works in every climate or site
Do not label a generic arcade as regionally authentic

title: Four-iwan courtyard
region: Iran and later adaptations across a wider region
period: Established in congregational mosque planning by the medieval period
summary: A courtyard organized by four vaulted halls, with the qibla iwan giving directional and spatial emphasis. Its logic is axial and volumetric—not merely an arch motif.
spatialPrinciples: Four iwans address a central courtyard
Qibla iwan establishes primary orientation
Layered movement from city edge to court to prayer space
climateAndMaterial: Courtyard microclimate needs project-specific simulation
Vault and dome concepts require qualified structural design
Brick, tile and surface systems need local supply and maintenance studies
designMoves: Use hierarchy to clarify qibla direction
Compare courtyard dimensions against capacity and circulation
Separate historical precedent study from contemporary code resolution
avoid: Do not reduce the lineage to four decorative arches
Do not transfer historic proportions without site analysis
Do not imply structural validity from a concept model

title: Ottoman central-dome composition
period: Developed through the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries and beyond
summary: A centralized prayer volume shaped by a major dome and supporting semi-domes or subsidiary volumes, commonly paired with a forecourt. The spatial and structural system comes before its silhouette.
spatialPrinciples: Strong centralized worship volume
Hierarchical dome and support system
Forecourt mediates arrival and congregational movement
climateAndMaterial: Large-span geometry requires professional structural and seismic analysis
High volumes require acoustic, thermal and maintenance strategies
Daylight openings must manage glare at prayer level
designMoves: Test speech intelligibility before formal refinement
Keep entrances and accessible circulation clear around central supports
Model maintenance access to high-level surfaces and systems
avoid: Do not begin with a dome silhouette detached from structure
Do not copy imperial scale into a community brief
Do not imply that formal resemblance establishes cultural legitimacy

title: Sudano-Sahelian earthen tradition
region: West African savanna and Sahel; locally distinct traditions
period: Living building traditions with documented historic examples
summary: Earthen mosque traditions shaped by local craft, climatic response, buttressed walls and recurring maintenance. Community knowledge and material cycles are central—not optional styling details.
spatialPrinciples: Massive earthen walls and buttressing shape enclosure
Roof and projecting timber can participate in maintenance systems
Form, craft practice and community stewardship are interdependent
climateAndMaterial: Soil, rainfall, drainage and roof detailing require local testing
Maintenance cycles must be funded and planned from the outset
Local craftspeople and conservation knowledge should guide material decisions
designMoves: Begin with water shedding, raised thresholds and site drainage
Document local soil mixes and repair practices
Budget recurring inspection and replastering as building care
avoid: Do not paste an earthen-looking skin onto an unrelated system
Do not treat diverse West African traditions as one uniform style
Do not specify an earth assembly without local material and structural expertise

title: Contemporary, locally grounded study
summary: A process for developing a mosque from worship, climate, community and local construction needs without claiming a historic lineage. Pattern is applied only after spatial and material decisions are understood.
spatialPrinciples: Qibla, prayer rows and inclusive access organize the plan
Community program and daily operation determine adjacencies
Structure and envelope remain renderer-neutral and exchangeable
climateAndMaterial: Use measured site climate and locally serviceable assemblies
Compare embodied impact, durability and repair access
Prototype screens and surface patterns for light, heat and cleaning
designMoves: Record why each precedent is relevant
Use pattern as a performance-capable layer where appropriate
Maintain a decision log and professional review gates
avoid: Do not call a new design traditional or authentic without accountable review
Do not use sacred text as decorative filler
Do not let visualization outrun structural, fire or accessibility review

title: Anatolian timber hypostyle
region: Medieval Anatolia; five UNESCO-listed living mosques
summary: Rows of timber columns support flat timber ceilings within masonry enclosures. The lineage joins structure, woodcraft and continuing community care rather than offering a decorative kit.
spatialPrinciples: Repeated timber-column prayer hall
Masonry outer enclosure with timber interior structure
Crafted ceilings, fittings and furnishings form a coordinated whole
climateAndMaterial: Timber species, moisture, fire, seismic and connection behavior require local evidence
Replacement and conservation strategies must distinguish structure from applied finish
Local craft capacity and inspection access shape feasibility
designMoves: Coordinate column spacing with prayer rows and sightlines
Expose inspectable connections and moisture risks
Plan craft samples and maintenance ownership before specification
avoid: Do not imitate historic carving without a documented reference and skilled authorship
Do not infer structural or fire performance from precedent
Do not treat five distinct mosques as interchangeable

title: Western Islamic hypostyle study
region: Al-Andalus, with wider western Islamic relationships
period: Great Mosque of Córdoba developed from the eighth century
summary: A repeated-bay prayer hall whose double-arched structural rhythm demonstrates spatial expansion and material hybridity. Study the system and history, not a horseshoe-arch silhouette.
spatialPrinciples: Expandable repeated-bay hall
Layered structural rhythm organizes interior movement
Courtyard and hall form a larger congregational sequence
climateAndMaterial: Arcades, roof and lateral stability require contemporary engineering
Deep interiors need daylight, wayfinding and acoustic analysis
Material reuse in historical precedent must not be copied without its cultural context
designMoves: Test repeatable bays as a phased-growth framework
Use structure to clarify rather than interrupt prayer rows
Study daylight gradients and accessible orientation through deep plans
avoid: Do not label generic arches Andalusi
Do not detach ornamental form from structural and historical context
Do not reproduce heritage fabric as a new authenticity claim

title: Indo-Islamic courtyard + screen study
region: Delhi and wider, locally varied Indo-Islamic traditions
period: From the late twelfth century in the cited Qutb complex
summary: A large arcaded courtyard and emphatic qibla-side screen illustrate translation between building traditions. It requires careful study of reuse, power, craft and local histories.
spatialPrinciples: Courtyard enclosed by arcades
Qibla-side screen establishes directional emphasis
Gateway, court and prayer edge create a staged sequence
climateAndMaterial: Stone craft and structural logic are project- and region-specific
Shade, heat, rain and crowd movement require current analysis
Historic spolia and cultural encounter demand critical interpretation
designMoves: Study thresholds and screens as spatial orientation devices
Compare shaded arcade depth with climate and gathering use
Record whose history and craft knowledge inform adaptation
avoid: Do not extract a screen motif from contested historical context
Do not call generic lattice work Mughal or Indian without evidence
Do not assume stone precedent validates a new assembly
